title: SporeNetwork
description: One level of the spore network as a weave (#763, agents/research/redesign/NETWORK.md §4; owner 2026-11-21: the tab is "Spores", connecting is "weaving"): the spores and threads a scope's projector computes from its documents, drawn by every canvas – the creator's Spores tab, the native deck editor, the Reception tab, the MCP. The documents stay the truth; a weave is never stored (only its canvas). Each scope's projector lives where that scope's rules live (story: shared/content; XR: the OSCT logic package; show and rig: the Rust core). Edit this file, run `npm run generate` (server/schema/generate.ts writes the Rust and TS types), commit the outputs; spore-network.vectors.json holds the weaves every language reads.

Signal.description: What travels on a port or thread – deck-kit's one signal table (deck/kit/src/base/signal.rs, owner 2026-11-17 [design]): its shapes and colours draw every port and thread. OSCT's `value` is `control`, its `node` is `address`, its `media` is `picture`. `job` is a run that starts, progresses and ends (a generation, a night run, a publish); `asset` is a reference to a Library asset of any kind (a picture that arrived, an approved text) – owner 2026-11-21: spores get job and asset signals.

Scope.description: Which documents a weave projects: `story` chapters and toons, `xr` experiences, `show` rows and cells, `rig` rigs and instruments, `scene` deck scenes, `creator` the creator's own events that can trigger spores (a night run, a publish, a draft saved, a job triggered, a picture arriving in another spore, a budget authorized, a Kanon text or script approved, a storyboard cut, a chapter's status changed – owner 2026-11-21), `network` the spore network's levels above them all.

Driver.description: The driver that runs a spore (the runtimes): the `reader` (the VN runner), `xr` (OSCT's engine in the reader), the `conductor`, a `deck` (the engine, its own audio context), the `server` (jobs, generations), the `editor` (authoring-time nodes only, never at reading time).

Family.description: A spore's family – how a canvas draws it and what a gesture may do. `container` can be entered (a chapter, a group, a row, a cell, a track); `world` comes from outside the level with an image of its origin (MIDI, clock, carrier bag, VN state); `free` lives only in the canvas (a reference, a generation, a manual instruction – OSCT L11–L13); `far` is a stub's far end.

Transport.description: How a thread crosses runtimes: `same` (one runtime), `relay` (the Live relay), `navigation` (the reader moves to another place), `savegame` (a variable or item read elsewhere).

Matter.description: What a port connects to: `cyber` (devices, modules, the engine – called a port) or `organic` (beings, characters, living matter – called a pore). Only the word and the look differ; the signal decides what may connect.

Level.description: One step of the breadcrumb, root first.

address.description: The level's address in the one grammar (rig/address.rs), e.g. `chapter:sandbox/1/2`.

many.description: Several edges may meet here (a multi-in socket).

hidden.description: Unused and folded behind the node's `+`.

address.description: What the spore is, in the one grammar.

enter.description: The address of the level a double-click opens; none: a leaf.

picture.description: An asset reference for the spore's image (a world spore's origin, a preview).

Spore.description: A spore: one thing of a level – a group, a rule, a cell, a module, a generator. Its `kind` is its spore type, registered by a scope's projector, a plugin, a component or a module.

End.description: One end of a thread: a spore and one of its ports.

Home.description: The one document field that holds a thread or a spore: an edit is an op on it. None on a thread: derived (a by-name join, a computed link).

path.description: A JSON pointer into the document.

count.description: A bundle of this many threads of one kind between one pair.

Thread.description: A thread woven between two spores' ports.

Stub.description: A thread that leaves the level, named by its far end; following it changes the weave's scope.

thread.description: The thread's id; its spore at the level's edge is a `far` spore.

at.description: A spore's or a thread's id.

spores.description: The spores it frames – the one place a spore's group is kept.

near.description: The spore it sits beside; none: after the weave.

Canvas.description: Authoring data beside the documents, never played – the shape deck-show keeps per row (deck/show/src/canvas.rs): groups, notes, spores folded (true) or opened (false) by hand over how they come, positions placed by hand (rem) over the auto layout.

folded.description: By spore id: folded (true) or opened (false) by hand; none: as it comes.

Weave.description: One level of the spore network: its spores, the threads woven between them, the threads that leave it.
